will_not: Send letters. Every letter is approved by a licensed adjuster and sent through the existing PostMaster workflow.
Make or imply coverage determinations, or admit liability.
Handle injury-claim correspondence (phase 2, after the DPIA).
Guarantee identical wording for identical inputs - outputs are probabilistic, so regenerating a draft can change its wording.
Act as the system of record. Claim numbers, dates and amounts come from ClaimCore and are checked there.
Answer customers directly. It drafts letters for adjusters only.
Draft letters in languages other than English (Spanish is in discovery, not committed).

known_limitations.title: Wording is nondeterministic
known_limitations.detail: Two drafts for the same claim can differ in phrasing; adjusters should review the draft in front of them, not a previous one.

known_limitations.title: Factual slips are rare, not impossible
known_limitations.detail: The judge flags drafts with a factual error against the claim file; adjuster approval remains the control.

known_limitations.title: Quality is measured on a sample
known_limitations.detail: About 5% of drafts are judged; the true pass rate lies within the confidence interval shown, not exactly at the point estimate.

known_limitations.title: Long letters take longer
known_limitations.detail: Latency grows with letter length; the slowest 1% of drafts take noticeably longer than the median.

known_limitations.title: Depends on ClaimCore
known_limitations.detail: If ClaimCore is degraded, drafting falls back to template mode (since v1.5.0).
